title: The artist, like the God of creation, remains within or behind or beyond or above his handiwork, invisible, refined out of existence, indifferent, paring his fingernails
html_source:
See Whitman for another version of the artist’s separation from his work.

See also the famous remark of the French novelist Gustave Flaubert, in an 1852 letter to his mistress Louise Colet:

An author in his book must be like God in the universe, present everywhere and visible nowhere.
